prerequisites.rationale_text: Practice without feedback is just repetition. Deliberate practice requires constant, high-quality feedback from the environment to correct errors, calibrate performance, and drive genuine mastery.
prerequisites.source_quote: DP thrives within environments that provide constant, high-quality feedback. Realistic practice incorporates feedback from the social and physical world, which is essential for achieving genuine mastery.

prerequisites.rationale_text: If you hold a fixed mindset (abilities are innate and unchangeable), deliberate practice seems pointless. Growth mindset — the belief that improvement is possible through effort — is the psychological foundation that makes DP worthwhile.
prerequisites.source_quote: competence is not an innate, vaguely defined ability but is achieved by accumulating and integrating a lot of specific skills and knowledge.

curation_notes.summary: Two prerequisites converge on DP: feedback-loops provides the mechanism (information about performance), growth-mindset provides the motivation (belief that practice can improve ability). Without either, DP degrades to mindless repetition or doesn't start at all.
